calls.reason: Altman's Reflections essay does discuss AGI without defining it, but the packet shows no named actor changing its own earlier criteria. The idea that people are dodging on purpose is rhetoric and can't be checked.

ARC Prize says o3 still failed easy tasks and wasn't AGI, but o3's 87.5% score and the Sparks paper show some arguments on the other side existed. 'Zero justification' is an evaluative judgment the evidence can't settle.

OpenAI's economic charter definition dates from 2018, before the claimed period. The Noema essay is a rival view, not a changed one. The packet doesn't clearly show 'a lot' of shifting after February 2023.

Business Insider, citing The Information, reported that Microsoft and OpenAI defined AGI as a system that can generate $100B in profits. That matches the core claim, though the deal was already signed, not just being considered.

OpenAI's own December 2024 system card shows o1 and GPT-4o making things up 20–30% of the time on questions about people. A 2023 test found GPT-4 made illegal moves in 32% of games and played far below grandmaster level.

Nadella's push for an economic-growth benchmark and Altman calling AGI 'not a super useful term' fit the prediction. But Altman still kept cognitive criteria, and the new expert panel only changes who verifies AGI. Mixed overall.
